findings.evidence: ConnectionMatrix.lean:64 is `public section`, not `@[expose] public section` as the PR description claims; the file itself must use the equation lemma in-module (`rw [IsNormalized.eq_1]`, line 172). Convention: Kernel/L2.lean:90-93 `l2inner_def ... := (rfl)` with the comment "the definition's body is not exposed across module boundaries".
findings.fix: Add the repo-standard unfolding lemmas `isIsoInvariant_iff`, `isReflectionPositive_iff`, `isMultiplicative_iff`, `isNormalized_iff` proved `:= Iff.rfl` (cf. `l2inner_def := (rfl)`), or mark the four defs `@[expose]`.
findings.issue: `IsIsoInvariant` (75), `IsReflectionPositive` (116), `IsMultiplicative` (122) and `IsNormalized` (127) are `def ... : Prop` inside a plain `public section` with no `@[expose]` and no unfolding lemma, so downstream (Layer 8b consumes all four as hypotheses) a term `h : IsNormalized f` is opaque: it can be neither applied nor proved. Only `IsReflectionPositive` has an eliminator (`posSemidef`), and even it has no introduction form.

findings.evidence: LabeledGraph.lean:428 `private noncomputable def glueCommEquiv`, 446/452 `private theorem glueCommEquiv_glueInl/_glueInr`; grep shows no public `glueCommIso_*` lemma, and ConnectionMatrix.lean:102 uses it only through `Nonempty`.
findings.fix: Add public `@[simp] theorem glueCommIso_glueInl (G₁ G₂) (a) : G₁.glueCommIso G₂ (G₁.glueInl G₂ a) = G₂.glueInr G₁ a` and the `glueCommIso_glueInr` mirror (statable entirely in public terms), derived from the private equiv lemmas.
findings.issue: `glueCommIso` is public but wholly opaque: its `toEquiv` is the private `glueCommEquiv`, and the lemmas that say what it does to vertices (`glueCommEquiv_glueInl` line 446, `glueCommEquiv_glueInr` line 452) are `private`. A consumer cannot compute or rewrite `glueCommIso G₁ G₂ v` at all; the only usable fact is `Nonempty (... ≃g ...)`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib has only `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.map_sup` (mathlib/Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Subgraph.lean:663); no pushforward `SimpleGraph.map_sup` exists. Precedent for a small general file: TauCeti/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Sum.lean.
findings.fix: Move it to a general home as a public lemma (e.g. a `TauCeti/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Maps.lean` next to the existing `TauCeti/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Sum.lean`) and import it here.
findings.issue: `private theorem map_sup {V W} (f : V → W) (G H : SimpleGraph V) : (G ⊔ H).map f = G.map f ⊔ H.map f` is general infrastructure — statement and proof mention only Mathlib types and do not touch labeled graphs — hidden as `private` in a Layer-8a file.

findings.evidence: grep in the repo shows no use of `glueLeft`/`glueRight`/`glueIndex`/`glueCarrier` outside LabeledGraph.lean; ConnectionMatrix.lean references only `glue`, `forgetLabels`, `glueCommIso`.
findings.fix: Mark `glueCarrier`, `glueIndex`, `glueLeft`, `glueRight` and their eight lemmas `private` (they are used only inside this file), keeping the `glueInl`/`glueInr` layer as the public surface.
findings.issue: The whole carrier layer is public although it serves only the construction of `glue`: `glueCarrier` (111), `glueIndex` (114), `glueLeft`/`glueRight` (120/125) and their lemmas `glueLeft_label`, `glueRight_label`, `glueLeft_of_unlabeled`, `glueRight_of_unlabeled`, `glueLeft_injective`, `glueRight_injective`, `glueLeft_eq_glueRight_iff`, `glueLeft_surjective_or` (129–220). Each duplicates a public `Fin`-level counterpart (`glueLeft_eq_glueRight_iff`/`glueInl_eq_glueInr_iff`, `glueLeft_surjective_or`/`glue_surjective`, `glueLeft_label`/`glueInl_label`), so the API ships twice under confusable names.

findings.evidence: No proof in ConnectionMatrix.lean unfolds these: `connectionMatrix` (83) only applies `.glue`/`.forgetLabels`, and `nonneg_glue_self` (145) uses the projections `.n`/`.graph`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[expose]` from `glue`, `glueInl`, `glueInr`; the characteristic lemmas above (plus the `glueCommIso_*` lemmas requested above) are the interface.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `glue` (226), `glueInl` (235) and `glueInr` (241) publishes bodies no consumer needs to unfold: the definitions are already pinned by `glue_graph`, `glue_card`, `glueInl_label`, `glueInr_label`, `glueInl_eq_glueInr_iff` and `glue_surjective`. Exposing them also leaks the carrier layer's `glueIndex`/`glueLeft`/`glueRight` into the public interface.

findings.evidence: ConnectionMatrix.lean:147 `simpa [connectionMatrix] using h` and 181 `simp [connectionMatrix, ...]` — the pinned entry law is never used by its own file.
findings.fix: Keep the roadmap-pinned `connectionMatrix_apply` but add (and `@[simp]`-tag) the normal-form entry law `connectionMatrix f A i j = f ((A i).glue (A j)).n ((A i).glue (A j)).graph`, and use it in `nonneg_glue_self`/`isReflectionPositive_one` instead of unfolding `connectionMatrix`.
findings.issue: The `@[simp]` entry law is stated in the `.forgetLabels.1 / .forgetLabels.2` form, which is not the simp normal form given the `@[simp]` lemmas `forgetLabels_fst`/`forgetLabels_snd` (LabeledGraph.lean:392-397); the file's own proof bypasses it and unfolds the definition instead (`simpa [connectionMatrix]`, line 147).

findings.evidence: grep `@[simp]` in LabeledGraph.lean returns lines 130, 138, 392, 396 only.
findings.fix: Tag `glue_card` (277) and `glueInl_eq_glueInr_iff` (252) `@[simp]`, and move the `@[simp]` markers off the carrier lemmas when they become private.
findings.issue: The public gluing API carries no `@[simp]` annotations at all — the only `@[simp]`s in the file sit on the internal carrier lemmas `glueLeft_label`/`glueRight_label` (130/138) — so `simp` cannot normalize `(G₁.glue G₂).n` or discharge `glueInl G₂ a = glueInr G₂ b`.

summary: The gluing surface is publicly complete on the pushout side, but four structural predicates ship as unexposed `def`s with no unfolding lemma (unusable downstream), `glueCommIso` has no public pointwise law, a general `SimpleGraph` lemma is hidden as `private`, and the internal carrier layer is public and duplicates the `glueInl`/`glueInr` API.
